prize_parts.citation: for showing how technological change and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B006 with Autor, Hanson and Katz as a single part. My confidence in the Katz name is lower than in round 1. Having read the exchange, I want the case to rest on the criteria and not on the fact that ten members converge. The scientific case has three parts. First, B006 pairs an explanatory framework (the supply-and-demand account of the skill premium, task-based views of work) with transparent local-labour-market designs for import competition. The framework says what to look for and the designs test it, so the two strands reinforce each other. Second, maturity is met. The skill-premium line is about three decades old, the task framework over twenty years, and the trade-shock papers over a decade. They have been replicated across countries and criticised hard, including in the shift-share inference literature. In my reading that scrutiny has qualified the magnitude and persistence of the effects but not the existence of sizeable local adjustment costs. Third, the credited names map to identifiable strands: Katz to the long-run wage-structure and skill-demand account, Autor to tasks and the trade-shock design, Hanson to the trade-shock evidence. On the chair's question about one discovery or two, I treat it as one achievement: showing how exposure to technology and trade shifts labour demand and who bears the adjustment costs. The citation is worded on that basis. It does not claim origination of the task framework, so Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu's theory are not implicitly credited or discredited. It states no settled long-run magnitude. It does not restate the 2023 prize on women's labour-market outcomes or the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity. I would regard it as sufficient for the committee to treat as established the effects on labour demand and local adjustment. Magnitude, persistence and external validity can stay open, because a contested size is not an unconfirmed finding. I keep B034 as my first alternative because its BLP core is cleanly attributed and mature. I keep B001 as the second.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution, and I weigh it more heavily after round 1. Dorn is a central co-author of the China-shock papers and is excluded only by the three-person cap. Several colleagues, including Strömberg and Teorell, describe Katz's claim as the most exposed or the closest call, because his best-known education-technology work is joint with a 2023 laureate. His separate wage-structure and skill-premium contributions carry my support for him, but I cannot show from my supplied evidence that they carry a distinct prize-sized claim. If the committee judges that the citation must be one tightly bounded discovery about trade-shock design, Autor, Dorn and Hanson is the cleaner fallback and I would accept it. A two-name Autor and Hanson prize avoids the Katz-versus-Dorn dilemma, but it would credit the trade-shock and task evidence more than the skill-premium account that interprets it. The shift-share and persistence debates are real, and the framing as one discovery is a judgement that others could reasonably reject. I also remain methodologically close to this ballot, so I may be too generous toward design-based evidence.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B007 first and B006 sixth. He would credit only Autor and Hanson for B006, reads the ballot as two related lines (tasks and skill demand versus import competition), and notes that Katz's education-technology work with Goldin sits alongside a prize already given in 2023.
responses.response: I take the two-lines reading seriously, and it is the best argument against my configuration. I land differently on the remedy. An Autor-Hanson pair credits the trade-shock and task evidence but drops the skill-premium account. That account is what makes the evidence a statement about labour demand and not only about local adjustment to one shock. I would handle the Goldin overlap through citation wording and a precise description of Katz's contribution, namely wage structure and the supply-and-demand account of the skill premium, and not by cutting the strand. I agree that if the committee cannot agree whether this is one discovery or two, the narrower Autor, Dorn and Hanson prize is more defensible than a pair that drops Dorn. I also agree that B007's attribution is cleaner. The reason I rank B006 above it is confirmation. The identification in B006 is design-based and has been tested against alternative specifications, while the constitutional and electoral-rule results are more assumption-sensitive, as you concede yourself.

responses.point: Strömberg calls Katz's marginal claim the most exposed part of the trio because of his work with a recent laureate. He names Autor, Dorn and Hanson as the natural fallback within the same discovery if the committee finds the Katz strand too entangled.
responses.response: I agree with the diagnosis and with the fallback. I disagree only on how much the Goldin joint work reduces his claim. The test I would apply is whether the skill-premium and wage-structure account has independent standing apart from the education-technology book. In my reading it does, because it is the framework through which the later task and trade-shock evidence is interpreted. I hold this with less than full confidence, because I cannot establish Katz's separate share from the evidence in front of me. I would change my configuration if colleagues showed that his independent wage-structure credit is thin relative to Dorn's role in the trade-shock designs. Absent that, the choice between the two versions turns on whether the committee wants one narrowly bounded discovery or one that spans the framework.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first after moving from B007. He names B007 as the first alternative, argues that its attribution is arguably cleaner than B006's, and discloses that Persson, a credited name on B007, is at his home institute.
responses.response: I accept that B007's attribution is cleaner, and I do not use your disclosed tie against the science. Per the chair's question, I do not think B007's case needs your vote to be heard. My reservation concerns the identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects and the closeness to the 2024 institutions prize, not the field. I would revisit it if the committee could show that the later quasi-experimental extensions and the state-capacity work carry the empirical weight, as Friberg suggests. I also note, given the chair's remark about convergence, that your move from B007 to B006 rests on the same criteria I am applying. I share your view that opening support counts should not be treated as merit.

responses.point: Dreber ranked B034 first in her opening and now prefers B006. She still regards BLP-style demand estimation and dynamic-oligopoly methods as a core contribution, transparent and reproducible, and keeps B034 as an alternative.
responses.response: We agree on B034's maturity and on the cleaner credit for Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. I treat it as my first alternative. I still weigh it below B006 because it is a toolkit whose reach into substantive findings runs through applications. I would not object if a colleague argued that a methods prize of this kind deserves equal weight. The chair asks whether anyone wants a two-part configuration. I do not, because the three-unique-people cap would force an unattractive split. A second part would leave one or two names on B006 or would give B034 one name, and neither division reflects the credit. A single B006 part is the more honest reading of the evidence.

uncertainties: Whether Katz or Dorn is the better third name, and whether Katz's separate wage-structure and skill-premium credit is large enough once the Goldin joint work is set aside.
Whether the committee reads technology and trade as one discovery about labour-demand adjustment or as two adjacent lines. If two, the Autor, Dorn and Hanson variant is the cleaner prize.

How far shift-share inference concerns and the persistence debate qualify the headline China-shock estimates, and whether a citation limited to effects on labour demand and local adjustment is enough.
Whether adjacency to the 2023 and 2024 prizes should affect timing even though the citations differ.
Whether my methodological proximity to this ballot leads me to overweight design-based evidence relative to B034 or B007.
statement.conflict_note: No co-authorship, institutional or collaborator tie to Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is apparent from my supplied profile. I disclose field proximity: I am an empirical labour economist working with Swedish register data and quasi-experimental designs, and my class-size work is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background. As chair, I also gave the 2021 presentation speech, which praised the credibility revolution; that speech reflects collective drafting and does not establish a preference. This is a methodological affinity that could bias my view of B006, and I have tried to apply the same criteria as for B034, B007 and other fields. I note, without adjudicating, the ties other members disclosed to one another: Krusell to Persson on B007, and the IIES and Stockholm links among Hassler, Krusell and Boppart. None of these is a tie to a B006 name.
